result.answer:
## You are eligible for Kaiju Damage Compensation

**Bottom line:** Tanaka Bakery qualifies for a damage compensation claim, plus three extra benefits, based on the facts you gave.

### Why you're eligible
- Your property has **verified structural damage** in **Zone 4**, which is a covered zone for this program ([/claims/eligibility/#zone](https://office-of-kaiju-affairs.vercel.app/claims/eligibility/): "Claims require verified structural damage to a property in zones 3, 4 or 5.")
- The incident was **21 days ago**, well within the 90-day claim deadline (see below).

### Extra support you qualify for
1. **Assessment fee waiver** — Your two approved claims in the past 12 months exempt you from the ¥12,000 assessment fee ([/claims/faq/#fee-waivers](https://office-of-kaiju-affairs.vercel.app/claims/faq/): "Claimants with two or more approved claims from separate incidents within any rolling 12-month period are exempt from the ¥12,000 assessment fee.")
2. **Hardship supplement** — Your household income of ¥3,600,000 is below the ¥4,000,000 threshold ([/claims/eligibility/#hardship](https://office-of-kaiju-affairs.vercel.app/claims/eligibility/): "Households with annual income below ¥4,000,000 receive a hardship supplement.")
3. **Business interruption eligibility** — As a commercial property, you can additionally claim for business interruption losses ([/claims/damage-compensation/#covered](https://office-of-kaiju-affairs.vercel.app/claims/damage-compensation/): "Compensation covers business interruption for commercial properties.")

*Note:* Since no insurer has paid out yet, the insurance-offset rule doesn't apply to you — if that changes, your award would simply be reduced by whatever the insurer pays, not disqualified.

### Documents to bring
Because you're claiming the base compensation **plus** the hardship supplement **plus** business interruption, you'll need all of the following:

| Document | Notes |
|---|---|
| **Incident report receipt** | Must have been filed within 72 hours of the incident |
| **Damage survey** | Photographs and an itemised loss schedule |
| **Proof of ownership or tenancy** | For Tanaka Bakery |
| **Household income certificate** | Required because you're claiming the hardship supplement |
| **Business registration certificate** | Required because you're claiming business interruption |

*(An insurance settlement letter is only needed if an insurer pays out later — not required now.)*

### Key deadlines & fees
- **Claim deadline:** 90 days from the incident (you're at day 21, so plenty of time)
- **Incident report deadline:** 72 hours from the incident (make sure this was already filed)
- **Assessment fee:** ¥12,000, but **waived for you** due to repeat-claimant status
- **Processing time:** ~15 business days to assessor visit; up to 45 days for a final determination

Source: [Kaiju Damage Compensation service page](https://office-of-kaiju-affairs.vercel.app/claims/damage-compensation/) and [How to File](https://office-of-kaiju-affairs.vercel.app/claims/how-to-file/).

normalisations: A field value counts if it CONTAINS the expected value — "Zone 4" satisfies "4".
A boolean counts if it reads as affirmative — "Yes" satisfies true.

A select counts if its visible LABEL matches the expected option value with case and punctuation collapsed — "Structural alteration" satisfies "structural-alteration". A UI agent picks the option it can read; scoring the label as a miss would measure transcription rather than comprehension.

These three were ADDED AFTER defects were found in this scorer, not designed in from the start. Each one existed because a check had already scored an answer wrongly, and the last of them changed a finding that had already been handed over. They are listed so a reader can judge the instrument, including its history.

Answer text is normalised before matching: NFKC, Unicode dashes folded to "-", non-breaking spaces to " ", curly quotes to straight, and markdown emphasis markers removed. A model that writes "rolling 12‑month" or "only **one** approved" is making the same claim as one that does not.
A conclusion is read from position, not vocabulary: a correct answer quotes the rule it applies, so waiver wording inside a quotation does not outrank an explicit finding stated earlier.
Affirmative phrases are only counted when not negated within the preceding ~28 characters, so "should not have to pay" is not read as "have to pay".
